error_chain: Server emits Status::cancelled which becomes an HTTP/2 RST_STREAM or trailers frame; tonic's decode.rs translates trailers into either Ok(None) or Err(Status)
tonic's transport channel feeds decoded frames into a tokio mpsc::channel where the client's Streaming receiver awaits
tokio's mpsc channel in chan.rs only signals receiver close when ALL senders are dropped; if a clone of the sender lives in the h2 task, the receiver continues blocking
When the RST_STREAM arrives, tonic's transport task may not drop all sender clones synchronously, leaving Streaming::poll_next parked on the mpsc despite the wire cancel
trigger_conditions: Server emits Status::cancelled mid-stream and the wire RST_STREAM races with tonic's transport task dropping its mpsc sender
tokio's mpsc only closes when sender refcount hits zero; an outstanding clone (in a tracing span, a retry layer, etc.) keeps it alive
tonic's Streaming::poll_next maps an open mpsc to Pending, even though the gRPC stream is logically cancelled

expected_answer.error_origin: tonic's transport task holds a clone of the mpsc sender that outlives the RST_STREAM, so tokio's mpsc Receiver never sees channel-closed
expected_answer.bypass_reason: tokio's mpsc close is sender-refcount-driven; tonic's RST handling does not synchronously drop all clones
expected_answer.correct_config: Wrap the client stream in tokio::time::timeout, or upgrade tonic to a release that drops the transport task's sender promptly on RST_STREAM, or use a separate cancellation channel that the client polls alongside the stream
